take_homes: An agent's output can't prove it's safe. You need a repeatable check, and the check can be an agent.
The risk loop is assess, mitigate, then write down the residual and accept it on record. That I can take to the board.
The agent audited our written policy rule by rule and flagged where it couldn't tell. I can put that in front of IT.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal what our policy says about finance data in an AI tool, then have my controller run the policy check on the variance-commentary pilot
monday.who: Controller, plus the IT security lead
monday.when: This week, before any pilot starts
monday.stop_condition: IT says no on finance data, or the check shows a rule the pilot breaks
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved the tool for finance data. I also still don't know the monthly cost for 40 people.

misconception.why: I saw the organisation's own policies turned into a repeatable check, which looks more like building something than buying a licence. We never covered cost or who owns the thing, so I'm still half-convinced it's a licence.

one_line: The first ten minutes were consultant filler. Then it ran our own policy against the agent and gave me a risk register with the residual written down, and that I'd show the board.
